description: I like music and numbers so I'm excited to combine the two and use sonification to bridge the two!
summary: This program uses data points from each decade from 1880 to the current year to curate a decibel depending on how high the temperature is and how low the temperature is. Based on how the temp was throughout the year, the interactive will emit a hymn of a pitch from the chorus Do, Re, Mi, Fa, So, La, Ti, Do,. "Data to my ears" is a project made with accessibility to audibility in mind. The temperature of the earth has been brought in many topics discussing the earth's future, and sometimes its hard to understand a graph with numbers and symbols. With this in mind, we decided to create a program that's interactive and accessible to people hard of sight, along with people who have an interest in the topic of our climate and its change throughout the decades and the centuries.
details: Our projects workflow starts off with the NASA dataset to then load the data, clean the data into a usable dataset, convert the numerical data values into pitches to generate audio notes into one track and export into a WAV file. The primary tools used were Python, Visual Studio Code, GitHub and data sources such as NASA GISTEMP Global Temperature and NASA Global Mean Sea Level datasets. Something our team considered was making a "Song of Earth" where we express datasets with a specific instrument and then bring it all together, but when we evaluated the data we had, we noticed that most of it followed a similar trend. So, there wouldn't be much variation between the instruments and predicted that it'd sound like instruments collectively playing higher and higher notes.
